column1: # usage-per-account.tsv — real account-usage readings, written from OUTSIDE the seats it measures (#1862).
# external crontab, never a PM seat's CronCreate — a ceiling-refused seat can't write). Reader:
# account -> seats companion block (one-time, Lead's ask). Seat->account is a function of
# CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, not seat name — verified by Pard 2026-09-23.
#   pipermorgan.ai:      arch cio comms cxo docs exec host lead pa ppm web  (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-pm; week resets Thu 22:00 PT)
#   designinproduct.com: pard janus + small projects                        (~/.claude; week resets Wed 21:00 PT)
# Size: 2 rows/reading x ~1-4 readings/day ~= <3k rows/year. Single file by design — do not "fix" into
# per-day rotation without cause; rotate only if cadence ever exceeds hourly.
# Readers MUST skip '#' lines. Rows are appended below the header; this block stays at the top.
# COLUMNS WIDENED 2026-09-24 ~13:2x (9 -> 12): scoped_model / scoped_pct / scoped_binding carry the
# per-model weekly limit that actually BINDS (Pard, 09-24: Fable 64% while the aggregate read 43% —
# the aggregate alone hid that the real constraint was three-fifths gone). scoped_binding = yes when
# that limit is the active one. Rows before the widening have 9 fields; awk-style readers cope, and
# scoped_* simply read empty for them. Failure rows keep the mode label in five_hour_pct (from 09-24
# 07:2x; earlier failure rows collapsed to UNMEASURABLE — their note holds the reader's real label).
